name: Zizilivakan
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: OLAC listing for ziz (2024 capture); SIL Cameroon resources browse-by-language; Glottolog 5.3 zizi1238; Crossref / theses.fr / archive.org probes
sources.note: No descriptive item anywhere: OLAC lists only Glottolog/Ethnologue/LinguistList records; silcam.org has no Zizilivakan resources; Crossref and theses.fr return 0 hits for 'Zizilivakan'; Meek 1931 (Fali of Jilbu vocabulary) is lending-only on archive.org.

sources.citation: Hoskison, James T. 1983. A Grammar and Dictionary of the Gude Language. PhD dissertation, Ohio State University (already held).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Not Zizilivakan, but the closest well-described relative (Gude-Jimi-Zizilivakan subgroup); the only available proxy for prosody in this cluster if the catalog ever admits genealogical proxies.

sources.citation: lexibank/kraftchadic (List, Forkel et al.): CLDF digitisation of Kraft 1981 wordlists; language 'Falijilbu' = zizi1238.
sources.note: Wordlist forms with tone marks only; Kraft's phonological notes are not included; cdstar object holds only the vol. I excerpt.

sources.citation: Garou, Abbo & Michael Etuge Apuge. 2024. Testing the Intelligibility of Nigerian Fali to Cameroonian Fali, Bana and Gude Listeners. Canadian Journal of Language and Literature Studies 4(2): 48-63. doi:10.53103/cjlls.v4i2.160
sources.note: Nothing on Zizilivakan phonology; states 'Nigerian Fali [incl. Fali of Jilbu] also does not have established linguistic data'; summarises Hoskison 1983 for Gude only (2 level tones).

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Table 3 lists 'Zizilivakan [ziz] Bata — none' (no lexical/descriptive source); sec. 3.3.1 uses only Kraft 1981 wordlist data for Zizilivakan (*ɮ retention); reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress; no stress statement for any Bata-group language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 486 Zizilivəkan.
sources.note: Nothing; entry gives names (Zilivə, ÀmZírív, Fali of Jilbu), location, classification; Refs. Dieu & Renaud (1983) only.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Michel Dieu. 2005 [2000]. Linguistique. In Seignobos & Iyébi-Mandjek (eds.), Atlas de la province Extrême-Nord Cameroun, 64-70. IRD Éditions. doi:10.4000/books.irdeditions.11562
sources.note: Nothing; one-sentence locational note on the 'Fali de Jilvu' language (few hundred speakers west of Guili, main area around Jilvu in Nigeria).

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Volume I (Plateau-Sahel). MSAA A 23. Berlin: Reimer. Introduction + TOC excerpt (17 pp., cdstar/lexibank).
sources.note: Nothing; describes entry format only ('a tentative phonemic inventory, several pages of notes on the phonology and six pages of the word lists').

sources.citation: van der Vloed, David et al. 2008-2010. Fali of Mubi Survey (SIL Nigeria / Luke Partnership): audio wordlist Zhilvu/Jilivu dialect of Zizilivakan, SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 51952 (and any unpublished survey report).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: 49-minute recorded 300+ item wordlist — the only audio of the language; would allow first-hand prominence judgments; an accompanying survey report, if it exists, is unarchived.

sources.citation: Bombay, Elaine. 2002. A report on Zizilivakan. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon (unpublished report, cited in Topics in Chadic Linguistics III, 2007).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other work devoted to the language; probably a rapid-appraisal sociolinguistic survey, but may contain a wordlist with transcription notes; not in SIL's public archive — request from SIL Cameroon (Yaoundé) library.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Volume III ("Biu-Mandara" et al.). Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde, Serie A: Afrika, Bd. 25. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. 'Fali Jilbu (Jilvu)' entry, pp. ~1-10 (cover page, tentative phonemic inventory, Notes, list).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological notes ever published on the language (phonemic analysis by M. J. Mould); need the Notes pages to confirm whether anything is said about stress/tone beyond the inventory (snippets suggest not). Google Books id YRy5AAAAIAAJ, no preview.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. I (chapter on the Fali, with Fali of Jilbu vocabulary). London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest data on Jilbu Fali; vocabulary only, very unlikely to mention accent, but the ethnographic preface occasionally comments on pronunciation.

sources.citation: van der Vloed, David (contributor). 2008-2010. Audio Wordlist: Fali of Mubi Survey, Zhilvu/Jilivu dialect [of Zizilivakan]. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 51952 (300+ item audio wordlist, draft).
